claims.text: What the strip looks like ST elevation in II, III and aVF, with reciprocal ST depression in aVL and Q waves developing in II, III and aVF.
claims.quote: ST elevation in leads II, III, aVF Hyperacute T waves may precede these changes Reciprocal ST depression in aVL Progressive development of Q waves in II, III, aVF

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) ST elevation: II, III, aVF; reciprocal depression in I, aVL; likely RCA (or LCx)
claims.quote: Inferior II, III, aVF I, aVL RCA (or LCx)

claims.text: Early sign: hyperacute T waves may come first
claims.quote: Hyperacute T waves may precede these changes

claims.text: aVL: the only lead truly reciprocal to the inferior wall — a sensitive marker of inferior infarction
claims.quote: aVL is the only lead truly reciprocal to the inferior wall, as it is the only lead facing the superior part of the ventricle. It is thus a sensitive marker for inferior infarction

claims.text: RCA vs LCx: ST elevation III > II, reciprocal depression in I, or signs of RV infarction suggest RCA; II = III, no reciprocal change in I, or lateral ST elevation suggest LCx
claims.quote: RCA occlusion is suggested by: ST elevation in lead III > lead II Presence of reciprocal ST depression in lead I Signs of right ventricular infarction: STE in V1 and V4R Circumflex occlusion is suggested by: ST elevation in lead II = lead III Absence of reciprocal ST depression in lead I Signs of lateral infarction: ST elevation in the lateral leads I and aVL or V5-6

claims.text: Rhythm: up to 20% develop second- or third-degree AV block
claims.quote: Up to 20% of patients with inferior STEMI will develop either second- or third-degree AV block.
claims.locator: Bradycardia and AV Block in inferior STEMI

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Artery: dominant RCA in 80%, dominant LCx in 18%, occasionally a wraparound LAD
claims.quote: Dominant right coronary artery (RCA) in 80% of cases Dominant left circumflex artery (LCx) in 18% Occasionally, a “type III” or “wraparound” left anterior descending artery (LAD)

claims.text: AV block mechanism: AV-node ischemia (its artery comes from the RCA 80% of the time) or the Bezold-Jarisch reflex (increased vagal tone)
claims.quote: Ischaemia of the AV node due to impaired blood flow via the AV nodal artery. This artery arises from the RCA 80% of the time, hence its involvement in inferior STEMI due to RCA occlusion. Bezold-Jarisch reflex = increased vagal tone secondary to ischaemia.
claims.locator: Bradycardia and AV Block in inferior STEMI

claims.text: Worse prognosis with: RV infarction (40%; may become severely hypotensive with nitrates), bradycardia from second- or third-degree AV block (20%), posterior extension
claims.quote: Associated features, all of which confer a worse prognosis, include: Concomitant right ventricular infarction (40% of patients); these patients may develop severe hypotension in response to nitrates Significant bradycardia due to second or third-degree AV block (20%) Posterior infarction due to extension of infarct area

claims.text: Symptoms Nausea and vomiting may occur, especially with inferior MI
claims.quote: Nausea and vomiting may occur, especially with inferior MI.
claims.locator: Symptoms and Signs of Acute MI

claims.text: Treatment As for STEMI: emergency PCI is preferred when it can be done in time (door-to-balloon < 90 minutes, < 120 with transfer) by an experienced operator
claims.quote: For patients with STEMI, emergency PCI is the preferred treatment of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction when available in a timely fashion (door to balloon-inflation time < 90 minutes, or < 120 minutes if hospital-to-hospital transfer is involved) by an experienced operator

claims.text: Bradyarrhythmias and AV block here are usually transient (hours to days), respond well to atropine and don't need permanent pacing
claims.quote: Bradyarrhythmias and AV block in the context of inferior STEMI are usually transient (lasting hours to days), respond well to atropine and do not require permanent pacing.
claims.locator: Bradycardia and AV Block in inferior STEMI

claims.text: With hypotension: get right-sided leads; if RV infarction is confirmed, avoid nitrates and diuretics
claims.quote: With hypotension after myocardial infarction or inferior STEMI, do ECG with right-sided leads to diagnose right ventricular infarction, and, if confirmed, avoid nitrates and diuretics.

notes.issue: claim dropped the quote's condition (timely, experienced operator)
notes.resolution: claim now says PCI is preferred when it can be done in time by an experienced operator; re-checked pass
